newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house panel approves oil bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house panel approves oil bill.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a bill opening up the country's petroleum industry to the private sector.
The bill was approved when more than half of the committee's 30 members voted in favor of the bill which now goes to the floor of the lower house for a vote. It must also be approved in the Senate.
In a final count, 23 members of the committee voted in favor of the bill, four against and three abstained.
The bill would allow private companies to compete with state-owned oil and gas giant Petrobras or to go into joint ventures with it.
The bill also creates the National Petroleum Agency, a regulator to oversee the petroleum sector, and the National Energy Policy Council, a government body responsible for energy policy.
The committee was due to vote on a series of amendments to the bill, one of which would strike down a clause that obliges the government to maintain a controlling stake in Petrobras.
